guide.summary: Private app on your own workspace (self-serve, wait none); Public app for other companies' workspaces (app review).
guide.verdict: Easiest: Private app on your own workspace (self-serve, wait none). Hardest: Public app for other companies' workspaces (app review).

composio.note: Composio lists a managed OAuth app for Intercom, fine for prototypes. For production, create a custom auth config with your own client ID and secret.

need_own_app.answer: Not for a prototype, since Composio offers a managed Intercom app. For production with your own branding, scopes and dedicated quota, yes, and customers outside your company need the app approved by Intercom.
reasons: Consent screen shows your app name instead of Composio
Managed app shares quota across all Composio users
Default scopes may not cover what you need
Managed auth enforces a 15-minute minimum trigger polling interval

scenarios.label: Private app on your own workspace
scenarios.when_this_applies: The agent only accesses data in your own paid Intercom workspace.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count, not measured

waiting.basis: c3 says no review is required for private apps.

scenarios.approval: No review for private apps that only access your own paid workspace data.

scenarios.label: Public app for other companies' workspaces
scenarios.when_this_applies: Customers outside your company connect their own Intercom workspaces via OAuth, listed or unlisted.

hands_on.basis: estimate from step count, not measured (demo video, listing, test credentials)

waiting.basis: No verified source backs this timeline (the agent's estimate was "Up to 7 business days per review round").

scenarios.approval: Intercom reviews every public app, listed or unlisted: scopes, OAuth flow in a video, and listing content.

modifiers.note: App stays private to your team until approved

extras: App stays private to your team until approved

prerequisites.title: Paid Intercom workspace and Developer Hub app
prerequisites.detail: OAuth is enabled by ticking Use OAuth on the Authentication page of a development workspace in the Developer Hub.

prerequisites.title: HTTPS redirect URL
prerequisites.detail: Redirect URLs must use HTTPS. Multiple can be added, the first is the default.

prerequisites.title: Test account or setup instructions
prerequisites.detail: If your service needs an account, give Intercom test credentials or set-up instructions.

steps.title: Enable OAuth in Developer Hub
steps.detail: Log in, open your app, tick Use OAuth on the Authentication page.
steps.done_when: client_id and client_secret visible on Basic Information page

steps.title: Choose minimal scopes
steps.detail: Draft a list of only the scopes the use case needs, with justification for each.

steps.title: Set scopes and redirect URL
steps.detail: Tick scopes on the Authorization page and add your HTTPS redirect URL.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config via Composio's API with your client ID and secret, using the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard.

steps.title: Record the OAuth demo video
steps.detail: Show install, full functionality, uninstall, and the full client_id and state in the OAuth URL.
steps.done_when: Video covers install, features and uninstall

steps.title: Prepare description and listing
steps.detail: Draft the app description, test instructions, and listing text meeting name and icon rules.

steps.title: Submit for review
steps.detail: In Test and publish, click Submit for Review.

steps.title: Wait for Intercom approval
steps.detail: Review can take up to seven business days; rejected apps must be fixed and resubmitted.

traps.title: Over-privileged scopes cause rejection
traps.detail: This is the most common reason for first rejection. Scopes beyond current functionality may force you to adjust and resubmit.

traps.title: Incomplete demo video means resubmission
traps.detail: If the video does not show all functionality and the OAuth processes, you must resubmit it.

traps.title: App name and icon rules
traps.detail: Names containing Intercom are not approved. Icon must be 512x512 PNG and cannot contain the Intercom logo.

traps.title: Wrong regional host fails for Google sign-in
traps.detail: Customers signing in with Google fail on the wrong regional host, so send them to the host matching their workspace region.

traps.title: Composio callback domain
traps.detail: Intercom's redirect URL is registered per app, but no domain verification was found in the dossier, so no proxy is required by the evidence.

blockers.what_it_means: Intercom asked for changes, for example to scopes, links or the video.
blockers.what_to_do: Make the requested changes and resubmit; another review of up to seven business days applies.
blockers.agent_can_help: Re-check scopes against functionality and draft a revised description.
